# Session Explorer

A session launcher for **OpenCode V2** — a fork of
[`ypxcs/opencode-session-history`](https://github.com/ypxcs/opencode-session-history)
that keeps the original terminal (TUI) history panel and adds a global Desktop
entry point: a titlebar button and a command that open a searchable dialog over
**every project and every archived session**, even from the home screen with no
session open.

Package: `opencode-session-explorer-desktop` · plugin id: `session-explorer` ·
repository: [wyattdave/opencode-session-explorer](https://github.com/wyattdave/opencode-session-explorer).

## What this fork adds

- **Global Desktop launcher.** A persistent titlebar button (`Sessions`) and the
  command **Session Explorer: Open** (`Ctrl+Shift+H` on Windows/Linux,
  `Cmd+Shift+H` on macOS). Both work on a cold-start home screen, with a draft,
  or with sessions open, and both call the same opener (no stacked dialogs, no
  DOM injection).
- **Native modal.** Built from `ctx.dialogs.open` + `ctx.ui`, large and
  responsive, search field focused on open, keyboard navigation, Enter to open,
  Escape to close, labelled listbox semantics for screen readers.
- **Complete metadata index.** Every root session on every connected server,
  archived and unarchived, fetched with cursor pagination (no fixed history cap)
  and searched client-side across title, project, directory, subpath, session ID
  and server name. No transcripts are read and no sessions are created just to
  enumerate them.
- **Filters and sorting.** Project dropdown with counts (including projects that
  only have archived sessions), All / Unarchived / Archived, sort by last
  updated / created / title with stable tie-breakers, and optional collapsible
  grouping by project.
- **Archive workflow.** Archive and restore from the row menu through the
  supported SDK mutation, verified by reading the session back. Running sessions
  cannot be archived. There is no delete action.
- **Safe navigation.** A row opens the session on its original server in a new
  focused tab, or focuses its existing tab. Archived sessions open directly on
  hosts that support it; otherwise the menu offers **Restore and open** (never a
  silent unarchive). A session whose working directory is confirmed missing asks
  before opening; an unknown directory state is never reported as missing.

The TUI and server entries are the upstream ones: same panel, same options and
defaults. `limit` only caps the TUI panel and never the Desktop list.

## Installation

Requires **OpenCode V2**. Desktop support was tested with OpenCode Desktop
**2.3.2** on Windows 11 (see [Version support](#version-support)).

The package is published to npm as `opencode-session-explorer-desktop` and ships
a prebuilt `dist/`, so consumers never run a build step.

### From npm

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-session-explorer-desktop
```

Or add it to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["opencode-session-explorer-desktop"]
}
```

Restart OpenCode Desktop.

### From a tarball or checkout

Useful before a release or when testing local changes.

```sh
# Somewhere outside the source tree, e.g. the plugins folder:
mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode/plugins/opencode-session-explorer
cd ~/.config/opencode/plugins/opencode-session-explorer
npm install /path/to/opencode-session-explorer-desktop-0.2.0.tgz
```

Then add the installed package to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`, merging it
with the entries already there:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    "C:/Users/you/.config/opencode/plugins/opencode-session-explorer/node_modules/opencode-session-explorer-desktop"
  ]
}
```

Restart OpenCode Desktop. `opencode plugin list` should show it:

```text
ID                VERSION  SOURCE
session-explorer  local    C:/Users/you/.config/opencode/plugins/opencode-session-explorer/node_modules/opencode-session-explorer-desktop
```

`opencode api plugin.list` additionally reports `state: active` and
`features: { server: true, tui: true, gui: true }`.

A checkout also works during development:

```jsonc
{ "plugins": ["C:/path/to/opencode-session-explorer"] }
```

> Git URL installs (`github:...`) fail on some V2 builds before the download
> finishes; prefer a local path or a tarball. Do not install the upstream
> package and this fork side by side — both register a history panel.

To uninstall, remove the `plugins` entry (or the folder) and restart. Removing
the plugin only removes its button, command and panel; it does not touch
sessions.

## Usage

### Opening the explorer

- Click the **Sessions** button in the titlebar (bottom-left, beside the status
  area). It is present on the home screen too.
- Press `Ctrl+Shift+H` (`Cmd+Shift+H` on macOS), or run **Session Explorer:
  Open** from the command palette / command menu.

The dialog opens with the search field focused. Escape closes it and returns
focus to where it was.

### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `↓` from the search field | Move into the results |
| `↑` / `↓` | Move between results |
| `Home` / `End` | First / last result |
| `Enter` | Open the highlighted session |
| `Esc` | Close the menu, then the dialog |

### Searching and filtering

- The search box matches title, project name, project directory, subpath,
  session ID and server name, case-insensitively. Typing is debounced, and the
  search runs over the complete in-memory index, so old archived sessions are
  found too.
- **Project** lists every project, with the number of matching sessions. Projects
  that only contain archived sessions stay in the list.
- **Session state** switches All / Unarchived / Archived. Archived results never
  depend on the unarchived page being loaded.
- **Sort by** offers Last updated (default), Created and Title. Ties break by
  session ID, so the order is stable.
- **Group by project** adds collapsible section headers with total counts; turn
  it off for the flat list.
- **Reset filters** returns project, state, sort, grouping and the search text to
  their defaults.
- Results load 200 rows at a time with **Show more**; there is no overall cap.

### Rows

Each row shows the title (`Untitled session` when blank), project, archived and
running badges, a directory-missing badge, the relative update time, and the
full directory in a tooltip. The row's `Open` action and the menu (`Archive`,
`Restore and open`, `Restore`, `Copy session ID`) never open the row by
accident.

- **Open** focuses the session's existing tab, or opens a new focused tab.
- **Archive** is disabled while the session is running.
- **Restore** puts an archived session back in the unarchived list.
- A confirmed-missing working directory triggers an **Open anyway** confirmation
  before the tab opens.

### Preferences

The project selection, archive filter, sort and grouping are stored in the
plugin's global store and restored on the next launch. A saved project that no
longer exists falls back to All projects. The search text is never stored, and
no transcripts, credentials or metadata caches are written to disk.

## Terminal (TUI) panel

The upstream sidebar panel is unchanged: it lists sessions newest-first, opens
one in the existing tab or a new tab, warns before opening a session whose
directory is gone, and refreshes from session lifecycle events. It is also shown
on the CLI home screen when the terminal is wide enough.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | `number` | `100` | Maximum number of sessions included in the panel list. Does not affect the Desktop explorer. |
| `maxVisibleSessions` | `number` | `3` | Sessions visible before the list scrolls. |
| `truncateSessionTitles` | `boolean` | `true` | Keep titles on one line with `...`. Set to `false` to word-wrap them. |
| `showMetrics` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the "Xm ago · $Y.YY" line under the title. |
| `showAllProjects` | `boolean` | `true` | When true, list sessions from every project. When false, only the current project's sessions are shown. |

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "C:/GitHub/opencode-archive-manager",
      "options": {
        "limit": 100,
        "maxVisibleSessions": 3,
        "truncateSessionTitles": true,
        "showMetrics": true,
        "showAllProjects": true
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> OpenCode passes a plugin's config `options` to its *server* half but not to its
> *TUI* half, which receives `{}` for a plugin declared in `opencode.json(c)`.
> The TUI reads the values back over the plugin's own `settings` RPC, so the
> table above still works from `opencode.json(c)`. Wrong-typed values are
> ignored rather than coerced.

For "open in a new tab" in the TUI, enable session tabs in `cli.json`:

```jsonc
{ "tabs": { "mode": "on" } }
```

## Version support

| Component | Version |
| --- | --- |
| Minimum and maximum tested host | OpenCode Desktop **2.3.2** (Windows 11, 2304×1536) |
| `@opencode/plugin` (host API used by the GUI entry) | 2.3.2 |
| `@opencode/client` | 2.3.2 |
| TUI peers | `@opentui/core` 0.9.3, `@opentui/solid` 0.9.3, `solid-js` 1.9.17 |

The Desktop plugin API is experimental: the GUI entry is published as
`./gui-experimental` and the host loads it as a prebuilt CJS bundle. Other host
versions have not been tested. On a host that marks the server incompatible, the
dialog lists it as incompatible and keeps working for compatible servers; it
never shows a failure as an empty archive.

## Troubleshooting

- **No Sessions button.** Check `opencode plugin list` for `session-explorer`
  with `features.gui: true`. A missing `gui` feature means the host did not load
  `./gui-experimental`; a plugin error is also logged to
  `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`.
- **"Connecting to the local server…" does not clear.** The dialog opened before
  the host listed its servers. It refreshes automatically once a server appears;
  otherwise use **Try again**.
- **Shortcut does nothing.** Another command may own `Ctrl+Shift+H`; reassign it
  in the host keybindings for the command id `session-explorer.open`.
- **An archived session opened but stayed archived.** That is the host's direct
  open path, and it preserves the archive. Use **Restore** in the row menu when
  you want it back in the unarchived list.
- **The dialog says the directory is missing.** The server reported that path as
  gone. Open anyway keeps the session but leaves the directory alone.
- **Manage the plugin in Desktop.** Settings → Extensions → Plugins shows the
  loaded plugin; reload after changing the config.

## Development

```sh
npm install          # or: bun install
npm run build        # Vite GUI bundle + the babel server/TUI build
npm run typecheck    # tsc --noEmit
npm test             # packaging/contract suite + pure explorer suite
npm run dev          # rebuild the GUI bundle on change
```

`npm run build` runs `vite build` (GUI → `dist/gui-experimental.cjs`) and then
`scripts/build.ts` (server/TUI → `dist/*.js`, `.cjs` preserved). `dist/` is
committed on purpose: package installs get no build step.

### Why the entries are prebuilt

OpenCode compiles plugin JSX through OpenTUI's Bun plugin, but that plugin skips
anything under `node_modules`, which is where package installs land. Bun's own
JSX transform then targets `@opentui/solid/jsx-runtime`, a static runtime: props
become plain values, and a signal read happens once at mount, leaving the panel
stale. `bun run build` therefore precompiles `src/**` with the transform OpenCode
would have applied (`babel-preset-solid`, `moduleName: "@opentui/solid"`,
`generate: "universal"`), and the compiled entry imports `@opentui/solid` and
`solid-js` by bare name so the host rewrites them to its own runtime.

The Desktop bundle is built with the official preset:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "vite"
import { gui } from "@opencode/plugin/gui/vite"

export default defineConfig({ plugins: [gui()] })
```

### Releasing

```sh
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm pack --dry-run   # inspect what the tarball will contain
npm publish          # requires npm credentials and the owner's approval
```

`prepublishOnly` re-runs the build, the typecheck and the tests. Commit `dist/`
before tagging: consumers never build.

## Limitations

- Only the built-in local server was available while testing. The code keys
  records by `(serverId, sessionId)` and isolates per-server errors, but a real
  two-server setup, an incompatible server, a dropped event stream and a
  disconnected server were not exercised in the app.
- The Desktop dialog was checked in the host's dark theme and in a 1000×1000
  window. Light theme and very small windows were not visually verified.
- The TUI panel was validated by the upstream test suite and the type/build
  checks; it was not driven interactively in a terminal during this round.
- Only the host versions listed above were tested; releases are cut by the
  repository owner.

# Session Explorer — implementation notes

This document records how the Desktop half of Session Explorer was built, which
host APIs were validated against the installed app, what was tested in the real
application, and what remains unverified.

Product: `opencode-session-explorer-desktop@0.2.0` (plugin id `session-explorer`).
Target host: **OpenCode Desktop / opencode v2.3.2** on Windows 11.

| Upstream commit | `2d61f0cd5205ef673fb547a3a5e7b454796c026b` (v0.1.5) |

| Working history | upstream commit `2d61f0c` is the base; the fork's changes are local commits on `main` |

## 3. Architecture

Three independent entries in one package:

```text
package.json exports
  ".":                 ./dist/index.js            server entry (upstream RPC + settings)
  "./tui":             ./dist/tui.js              terminal panel (upstream, precompiled)
  "./gui-experimental": ./dist/gui-experimental.cjs  Desktop GUI (new, prebuilt CJS)
```

```text
src/
  index.ts            upstream server registration (id renamed)
  rpc.ts              upstream RPC contracts (SessionHistory.check / settings)
  directory.ts        upstream server-side directory checks
  options.ts          upstream panel options + defaults (unchanged)
  sessions.ts         upstream pure session helpers (TUI)
  tui.tsx             upstream terminal panel (unchanged behaviour)
  explorer.ts         NEW: pure Desktop data layer (normalize/sort/filter/group/prefs)
  gui.tsx             NEW: Plugin.define({ stores, i18n, setup })
  gui/
    window.tsx        registrations (Style, Command, TitlebarItem) + dialog opener
    definition.ts     store schema + English strings
    preferences.ts    read/write/reset stored UI preferences
    controller.ts     state, refresh/generation/abort, events, mutations, navigation
    session-service.ts typed SDK adapter per server (paging, projects, running, dirs)
    SessionExplorer.tsx  dialog content, keyboard, a11y, paging, grouping
    SessionFilters.tsx   project/state/sort/group/reset/refresh controls
    SessionRow.tsx       row content, Open action, row menu
    styles.ts            injected CSS (host theme tokens only)
scripts/build.ts      upstream babel build, extended to skip src/gui* and keep the CJS bundle
vite.config.ts        official `gui()` preset
tests/run.ts          packaging + contract assertions (upstream tests extended)
tests/explorer.ts     pure data-layer assertions + a fake-client SDK adapter suite
```

The Desktop half imports only `@opencode/plugin/gui` and `solid-js`; it never
imports `@opentui/*`. The TUI half never imports the GUI runtime. Shared logic
lives in `src/explorer.ts` and is plain TypeScript (no DOM, no host imports).

### Data flow

1. `setup(ctx)` builds one controller for the window. Nothing is fetched until
   the dialog content mounts (`controller.open()`).
2. `refresh()` snapshots `ctx.servers.list()`, keeps each server's previous rows,
   and loads every compatible server in parallel.
3. Per server: `project.list({})` + `project.list({ archived: true })` and
   `session.active()` are read first; then root sessions (`parentID: null`) are
   paged with `order: "desc", limit: 100` for `archived: false` followed by
   `archived: true`, following `cursor.next` to exhaustion.
4. Each page is merged into the in-memory index and published immediately, so
   the dialog fills progressively.
5. When paging finishes, that server's directories are checked through the
   upstream `SessionHistory.check` RPC on the *same* server, in chunks of 500;
   results mark rows `present`/`missing` and everything else stays `unknown`.
6. `rows()` is the index; the dialog derives projects, counts, filtered rows,
   groups and the visible window from it with memoized helpers.
7. Searches are local over the complete index (debounced 180 ms). Sort and
   filter are local too, so nothing can be lost to a "first page only" search.

### State, races and cleanup

- Every `refresh()` increments a generation counter and aborts the previous
  request controller; results from a stale generation are dropped, so a slow
  response can never overwrite a newer query.
- Event-driven refreshes are debounced 300 ms. While the dialog is closed, events
  only mark the cache stale; the next open refreshes.
- Subscriptions are `createKeyed` over the sorted server-id list, so adding or
  dropping a server re-subscribes, and `onCleanup` stops each server's
  `data.listen` handle.
- A failed server load keeps that server's last good rows, marks the server
  `error`, shows a partial-results banner with **Try again**, and never renders as
  an empty archive.
- An empty server list is a "connecting" state (cold start), not an error.
- `ctx.servers.get(id).compatible === false` produces an incompatible-server
  banner and the server is excluded from loading.

## 4. Validated host API calls

Everything below was checked against `node_modules/@opencode/plugin` 2.3.2 and
then observed in the running Desktop app.

| API | Use | Observed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Plugin.define({ stores, i18n, setup })` | GUI entry default export | Bundle loaded by the host from `./gui-experimental` |
| `ctx.add(TitlebarItem, () => ({ id, label, title, icon, run }))` | global launcher | Pill "Sessions" rendered on home screen and sessions; click opens dialog |
| `ctx.add(Command, () => ({ id, title, description, keywords, group, section, bind, featured, run }))` | command | Command menu lists `Session Explorer: Open … CTRL SHIFT H`; id is `session-explorer.open` |
| `ctx.add(Style, css)` | styles | Injected once; removed with the window |
| `ctx.dialogs.open(render)` → `DialogHandle` | modal | Returns a handle; `.close()` dismisses |
| `ctx.dialogs.confirm({ title, description, confirm, cancel })` | missing directory | Resolves `true`/`false`; Cancel keeps the dialog, Open anyway proceeds |
| `ctx.dialogs.active()` | — | **Not used.** It stays `true` through the closing animation (see §6) |
| `ctx.ui.Dialog` (`title`, `size`, `footer`) | modal frame | Without it the content renders unframed and a backdrop click dismisses |
| `ctx.ui.TextInput`, `Select`, `Switch`, `Button`, `Menu`, `Loader`, `Icon` | controls | All render, keyboard-operable, themed |
| `usePlugin<typeof definition>()` | component context | Gives `ui`, `t`, `stores`, `toast`, `system`, `tabs`, `dialogs` |
| `ctx.t(key, params)` | labels | Strings resolve; `{{…}}` interpolates |
| `ctx.toast.show({ title, description, variant })` | feedback | Archive/restore/copy toasts confirmed |
| `ctx.system.copy(text)` | Copy session ID | Clipboard write succeeds |
| `ctx.stores.prefs.value` / `.set()` | UI preferences | Survives restart; `Store.global(schema, {}, [legacyKey])` imported an older key |
| `ctx.servers.list()` / `ctx.servers.get(id)` | server discovery | Returns `ServerRef { id, name, connected, compatible, client, data }`; empty during cold start |
| `ctx.tabs.list()` / `.open({ server, id }, { focus: true })` / `.focus(key)` | navigation | Existing tab focused; otherwise new focused tab; dialog closes |
| `server.data.listen(handler)` | live refresh | External archive/restore updated the open dialog without a manual refresh |
| `client.session.list({ order, limit, parentID, archived, cursor }, { signal })` | enumeration | `{ data, cursor: { next } }`; returns sessions across projects when `directory`/`project` are omitted |
| `client.project.list({})` / `({ archived: true })` | project names | Merged by id; failures are non-fatal |
| `client.session.active({ signal })` | running badge | `{ [sessionID]: { type: "running" \| … } }` |
| `client.session.get({ sessionID })` | read-back | `time.archived` present ⇒ archived |
| `client.session.update({ sessionID, archived })` | archive/restore | Accepted; state verified by the read-back |
| `client.rpc(SessionHistory).check({ directories }, { signal })` | missing directories | `{ missing: string[] }` from the owning server |

### Semantics verified during the spike

- `session.list` omits parent and project filters when they are not passed, so a
  single call returns sessions from every project/directory on that server
  (28 projects observed).
- `archived` is **not** a plain boolean field on the wire: `time.archived` is the
  marker. A restored session simply has no `time.archived`.
- `session.list` alone does not return both archive states; `false` and `true`
  were fetched separately and merged.
- The archived list is longer than the unarchived one (90 vs 4 root sessions in
  this instance); projects that only had archived sessions still appeared.
- The host opens archived sessions directly and keeps them archived; no
  unarchive happens on browse or open.
- `session.update` with `{ archived: false }` removes the archive marker and
  leaves id/project/history intact.
- Archived sessions with a deleted working directory are still openable after the
  warning; the directory is never recreated.

## 5. UI and accessibility decisions

- The dialog content is rendered inside `<ui.Dialog title size="x-large" footer>`
  so the host supplies the frame, header, close button, focus trap and Escape
  handling. The footer carries "Showing X of Y" plus **Show more**.
- Search is autofocused on mount (explicit `input.focus()` after the portal
  attaches, because `autofocus` alone loses to dialog focus).
- Keyboard: `↓` from search moves into the results, arrows move, `Home`/`End`
  jump, `Enter` opens, `Esc` closes. The results container is
  `role="listbox"` with `aria-activedescendant`; rows are `role="option"` with
  `aria-selected`. A visually hidden help paragraph is wired with
  `aria-describedby`.
- The row's click handler ignores events whose target is inside
  `.se-row-actions`, because Solid delegates `click` in the capture phase and a
  nested `stopPropagation` would run too late. The menu therefore never opens the
  row.
- Project keys used as `ui.Select` values are URL-encoded
  (`encodeURIComponent(serverId)+encodeURIComponent(projectId)`). A raw `\n`
  separator in a select value broke the host's DOM lookup and dismissed the
  dialog.
- All colors, borders and radii come from host/theme CSS variables, so the
  dialog follows light/dark theme and accent color. A media query tightens the
  layout for narrow windows; the results area is `min(54vh, 430px)` tall with a
  minimum of 180 px.
- Rows render in windows of 200 (not the full index) and use
  `content-visibility: auto`, which keeps thousands of rows cheap without
  pulling in a virtual list library. This is "incremental rendering", not true
  virtualization; revisit if a user reports jank at several thousand sessions.
- No DOM injection outside the plugin's own dialog, no host patching, no
  Electron main-process access, no SQLite access, no extra web server.

## 6. Defects found in the real app and fixed

1. **Frameless dialog / click-through.** Content passed straight to
   `ctx.dialogs.open` rendered without the modal frame and any click dismissed
   it. Fix: wrap everything in `ctx.ui.Dialog` with a title, size and footer.
2. **Project selection closed the dialog.** Project keys contained a newline;
   the host's select uses values for DOM lookup. Fix: URL-encode both halves.
3. **Escape-then-reopen did nothing.** The opener consulted
   `ctx.dialogs.active()`, which stays true during the closing animation. Fix: a
   private `showing` flag plus a 750 ms recovery timer for a render the host
   discards.
4. **Row-menu click opened the row.** `stopPropagation` inside the row came too
   late in Solid's capture-phase delegation. Fix: ignore clicks whose target is
   inside `.se-row-actions`.
5. **Repeated maps/tooltips were not announced.** Rows were buttons inside a
   nested `role="list"`; the nested list roles were removed so the listbox/option
   pairing is correct.

## 10. Blockers and limitations

- **No blockers** for the release gate: an archived session in another project
  opens directly from the home screen with no session previously open, and stays
  archived.
- The Desktop GUI API is experimental and version-pinned. The host assigns the
  GUI half the server plugin's id; the GUI bundle therefore declares no id.
- The host gives no focus API for an already-open dialog, so a second activation
  is ignored rather than re-focused.
- "Restore and open" cannot be exercised on this host because archived sessions
  open directly. The path is implemented (restore → verify → open) and falls back
  only when direct opening fails or the user chooses it.
- Liveness of an already-open dialog after a server restart was only observed via
  external mutations, not a killed server.
- `content-visibility: auto` means UIA exposes only the on-screen rows; this is
  expected, not missing data ("Showing 93 of 93").

## 11. Repro / rollback

- Rebuild: `npx bun run typecheck`, `npx vite build`, `npx bun run scripts/build.ts`,
  `npm test`, `npm pack`.
- Reinstall: copy the tarball into the plugins folder, `npm install <tarball>`,
  restart Desktop.
- Rollback: restore `opencode.jsonc.bak-session-explorer` (or delete the plugin
  entry) and restart. Removing the plugin changes no session data.
- Logs: `C:\Users\<you>\.local\share\opencode\log\opencode.log`.

# Security Policy

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please do **not** open a public issue for security problems.

Report privately through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting:

1. Go to <https://github.com/ypxcs/opencode-session-history/security/advisories/new>
2. Describe the issue, the impact, and steps to reproduce.

If that is unavailable, open a minimal issue that only asks for a private
contact channel — do not include exploit details.

## Scope

This plugin runs inside the OpenCode process and can read session metadata and
filesystem paths. Relevant reports include, but are not limited to:

- Reading or exposing data beyond the configured OpenCode server.
- Path handling that could escape the intended session/project directory.
- Any code path that executes untrusted input.

## Exposed surface

The plugin registers one RPC, `session-history.check`, which reports whether
paths supplied by the caller exist (and are directories) on the server. It
requires API authentication, returns no file contents and no directory
listings, and is strictly less information than the server's own `fs.read`,
`fs.list` and `fs.find` routes. Requests are deduplicated, capped at 1000
directories, and checked with bounded concurrency.

## Supported versions

Only the latest published version is supported. Please reproduce against the
latest release before reporting.
